uncited: Grid-Based Simulation maps physical sources (fluids, smoke, fire) into a discrete volumetric representation by solving partial differential equations on a structured spatial domain [S1, S2].

It differs from particle-based siblings like [Gaussian Splashing](1387-gaussian-splashing.md) and [Position Based Fluids](1765-position-based-fluids.md) by storing state in fixed voxel arrays, enabling efficient divergence and advection calculations via 3D textures [S1].
**State Storage**: Scalar fields (density $\rho$, pressure $p$, temperature $T$) and vector fields (velocity $u$) are stored in dedicated textures or arrays [S1, S2].

**Navier-Stokes Solver**: Most methods solve the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations to propagate velocity, typically using a projection method (advection, diffusion, force application, pressure projection) [S1].
**Advection**: Transport of attributes (smoke, fuel, velocity) is performed using semi-Lagrangian tracing or finite differences [S1].
**Rendering Interface**: The resulting grid serves as a volumetric texture container for ray marching or voxel rasterization [S1, S2].
It has been adapted for real-time graphics to simulate smoke, fire, and water by leveraging GPU compute shaders for the Navier-Stokes solver [S1].
